question.questionText: I saw her _______ a car.
question.explanationHtml:
Detailed Explanation:
In this sentence, 'I saw her _______ a car.', the verb 'see' is a perception verb. When perception verbs like 'see', 'hear', 'watch', 'notice', etc. are followed by an object (her), we use either the bare infinitive (base form of the verb) or the present participle (V-ing) depending on the meaning. The bare infinitive is used to indicate that the action was seen as a whole (from start to finish), while the present participle (V-ing) is used to indicate that the action was in progress (ongoing) when it was seen. In this context, both 'drive' (bare infinitive) and 'driving' (V-ing) could be grammatically possible, but only 'driving' is among the options. The correct answer is 'driving' (C), which means the speaker saw her while she was in the process of driving a car.
  • driven (V-ed (past participle)): Past participle form of 'drive', used in passive voice or perfect tenses, not suitable here.
  • drove (V2 (simple past)): Simple past form of 'drive', not used after perception verbs like 'see'.
  • driving (V-ing (present participle)): Present participle (V-ing), used after perception verbs to show an ongoing action.
  • to drive (to-infinitive): To-infinitive, not used after perception verbs like 'see'.
Related structure or vocabulary: Perception verbs (see, hear, watch, notice, etc.) + object + V-ing: to indicate an action in progress. Example: I saw him crossing the street.

Nếu muốn nhấn mạnh hành động đang diễn ra (đang lái xe), ta dùng V-ing. Nếu muốn nói đã nhìn thấy toàn bộ hành động, dùng động từ nguyên mẫu không 'to'. Trong các đáp án, chỉ có 'driving' (V-ing) phù hợp, nghĩa là tôi nhìn thấy cô ấy khi cô ấy đang lái xe.
  • driven (V-ed (quá khứ phân từ)): Dạng quá khứ phân từ của 'drive', dùng trong câu bị động hoặc thì hoàn thành, không phù hợp ở đây.

  • to drive (to-infinitive): Động từ nguyên mẫu có 'to', không dùng sau động từ chỉ giác quan như 'see'.
